newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port dispute continues but work to resume.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port dispute continues but work to resume.

text.p: Brazilian portworkers at the country's key port of Santos will return to work at 0700 local/1000 GMT Friday after staging a 24-hour protest over a delay in receiving their April salary, a union official said.

However a decision on whether or not to stage a full-out strike will depend on the outcome of discussions being held tonight between union officials and port authority representatives, said the local Port Operators' Union official.

Workers stopped work this morning after the CODESP port authority had deposited only 65 percent of workers' April salary in banks due to cash-flow problems stemming from a four-day stevedores strike last month.

Today the port authority paid the remaining 35 percent. However 30 percent of the workforce also normally receive an additional amount related to performance and only part of this had been deposited, a port authority spokeswoman said.
A meeting between union and port authority officials to discuss the performance-related pay was still continuing at 2130 local/0030 GMT.
"If nothing is resolved at this meeting, we will have an assembly and see if members want to take further action," the official said.
Unions if they wish to strike must give the port authority 72 hours notice so any strike would only take place next week, he added.
